title: En manos de: quién controla algo

sections.content: En manos de (in the hands of) names who owns or controls something -- vivid and common in describing shifts of ownership or power, like state assets moving to private control. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Menem puso en manos privadas empresas que llevaban décadas en manos del Estado.
items.english: Menem put into private hands companies that had been in the state's hands for decades.

items.spanish: Salinas devolvió a manos privadas la mayoría de los bancos comerciales nacionalizados en 1982.
items.english: Salinas returned to private hands most of the commercial banks nationalized in 1982.

items.spanish: Sectores estratégicos que habían estado en manos del Estado pasaron a estar en manos de inversores privados.
items.english: Strategic sectors that had been in state hands came to be in the hands of private investors.

items.spanish: Muchas de estas empresas terminaron en manos de inversores extranjeros, no de capital nacional.
items.english: Many of these companies ended up in the hands of foreign investors, not domestic capital.

sections.content: En manos de works equally well for people, institutions, or governments -- pair it with pasar a, quedar, or estar to describe a transfer of control or a current state of ownership.
